lines.japanese: 「よ、よしっ……入るぞぉー……」
lines.english: “A-all right... I'm going in...”

lines.japanese: 両手でパンパンと頬を二度叩いて表情筋を引きしめ、咳払いで滑らかな声の通りを確保。
lines.english: I slapped both cheeks twice to tighten my face, then cleared my throat to make sure my voice would come out smoothly.

lines.japanese: 「ぬるっと行こう！」
lines.english: “Smooth and slippery!”

lines.japanese: 「どもー！　お世話になりまーす！」
lines.english: “Morning! Glad to be here!”

lines.japanese: 俺はアレキサンダーのドアを開け、薄くクリスマスソングのかかった店内に足を踏みいれました。
lines.english: I opened Alexander’s door and stepped into the restaurant, where Christmas music played faintly in the background.

lines.japanese: しかしいつものように、カウンター席のしゃれたスツールへは向かいません。なぜなら、今日からお客様ではないからです。
lines.english: This time, however, I did not head for one of the stylish stools at the counter. As of today, I was no longer a customer.

lines.japanese: 「あー千歳君、いらっしゃぁい──」
lines.english: “Oh, Shusuke! Welcooome—”

lines.japanese: 「──じゃなかった。おはよー」
lines.english: “—No, wait. Good morning.”

lines.japanese: 「おはよざっす！　本日よりお世話になります、千歳鷲介です！　よろしくお願いします！」
lines.english: “Morning! Shusuke Chitose, reporting for my first day! Glad to be working with you!”

lines.japanese: 温かく迎えてくれた先輩スタッフに、体育会系のきちんとした挨拶。
lines.english: I gave the senior coworker who had welcomed me so warmly a crisp, sports-team greeting.

lines.japanese: いつものように、好きな言葉やら好きな天然記念物やらのしょーもない小ネタは挟みません。なぜなら、今日からお客様ではないからです。
lines.english: Unlike usual, I slipped in no feeble little jokes about my favorite word or favorite natural monument. As of today, I was no longer a customer.

lines.japanese: 「えー、そんな畏まらないでいいよう。いつも通りで、いつも通りで」
lines.english: “Oh, you don’t have to be so formal. Just act like you always do. Like always.”

lines.japanese: 井戸端会議のおばちゃんみたいに手をぱたぱたと振る紀奈子さん。
lines.english: Kinako fluttered both hands like a neighborhood auntie chatting over the fence.

lines.japanese: 「あざーす！」
lines.english: “Thank you!”

lines.japanese: そう言っていただけるととても気が楽になりますけど、まあ、他の先輩方の目もありますゆえ、慣れるまでは猫をかぶっていることにいたします。
lines.english: That certainly made me feel much more at ease. Still, with the other veteran employees watching, I would stay on my best behavior until I found my footing.

lines.japanese: だって、ねえ、初日にうざいキャラで認識されちゃったら、以降それで定着しちゃいますしねえ。無難に無難に。
lines.english: If they decided on my first day that I was the irritating one, the label would stick forever. Keep it bland. Keep it safe.

lines.japanese: 無難に──そう、それが俺のささやかな願望。
lines.english: Inoffensive—yes, that was my modest wish.

lines.japanese: 「でも、せっかく千歳君が入ってくれたのに、私ほとんど一緒に働けなくて残念だい」
lines.english: “But it's such a shame. You've finally joined us, and I'll hardly get to work with you at all.”

lines.japanese: 「そっすよねえ、紀奈子さんは今月いっぱいでしたっけ？　えーと、あと三日か」
lines.english: “Right. You’re only here through the end of the month, aren’t you? Let’s see, three more days.”

lines.japanese: 「ううん。このお店、木曜定休だから。実はもう、今日と明日で最後なんさー」
lines.english: “No. We close Thursdays, remember? Today and tomorrow are actually my last two days.”

lines.japanese: 「二日だけのロマンス！」
lines.english: “A romance lasting only two days!”

lines.japanese: 「私がいなくなったあと、えりちゃんとひよちゃんがこうならないか心配だったけど──」
lines.english: “I was worried that once I left, Eriko and Hiyo might end up like this—”

lines.japanese: 紀奈子さんは両手の人差し指を刀剣に見立てて、ちんちんと交差させました。
lines.english: Kinako turned both index fingers into swords and crossed them with a tiny ching-ching.

lines.japanese: 「──千歳君が上手くあいだに入ってあげてね」
lines.english: “—so make sure you step in between them and keep the peace, okay?”

lines.japanese: 「は、はい、善処いたします」
lines.english: “Y-yes. I'll do what I can.”

lines.japanese: いきなり難題だなあ──
lines.english: Talk about dropping a tall order on me—

lines.japanese: ──っと、カウンターの向こうでマスターが手招きしています。
lines.english: —and now the boss was beckoning from behind the counter.

lines.japanese: 「おい、そこの新入り」
lines.english: “You there. New boy.”

lines.japanese: 「はいっ」
lines.english: “Sir!”

lines.japanese: 俺は紀奈子さんに会釈を残してから、お客様の迷惑にならない程度の速足で雇用主のもとへ向かいました。
lines.english: I left Kinako with a bow, then hurried toward my employer as fast as I could without disturbing the customers.

lines.japanese: 初めて通されたカウンターの内側。そこから眺める店内の構図はちょっと新鮮です。
lines.english: It was my first time behind the counter. From there, the whole composition of the restaurant looked curiously new.

lines.japanese: 「おうい、みんなー。仕事しながらちょっと聞いてくれー」
lines.english: “Hey, everyone! Keep working, but listen up for a second!”

lines.japanese: マスターは俺の横に立って、厨房とフロアの従業員たちに呼びかけました。
lines.english: The boss stood beside me and addressed the employees in the kitchen and on the floor.

lines.japanese: 「えー、事前に話しておいたとおり、クリスマスシーズンの繁忙期に備え、非常勤のヘルプという形で手伝ってもらうことになった千歳君だ」
lines.english: “As I explained beforehand, this is Chitose, who'll be helping us on a casual basis through the Christmas rush.”

lines.japanese: 「はじめまして千歳鷲介です！　よろしくお願いします！」
lines.english: “I'm Shusuke Chitose. It's a pleasure to meet you. Glad to be working with you!”

lines.japanese: 礼儀を弁えつつも親しみの持てるキャラクターで売りだすため、俺はへこへこ機敏に頭を下げながら、挨拶まわりの新人アイドルみたいな愛想笑いを振りまきました。
lines.english: Aiming to market myself as courteous yet approachable, I bobbed my head briskly and scattered professional smiles like a rookie idol making the rounds to introduce himself.

lines.japanese: 「千歳君は他のアルバイトも抱えていて忙しい身なのだが、今回は俺の方から無理を言って頼みこんだんだ。よって彼の出勤日は任意ということになるが、まあ、君たちより時給も低い、僻まないでやってくれ」
lines.english: “Mr. Chitose is a busy man with several other part-time jobs, but I prevailed upon him to help us. His shifts will therefore be at his discretion. His hourly wage is lower than yours, however, so try not to resent him.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、そのほか細かい挨拶等は、休憩時間にでも各自適当に済ませるよう。以上」
lines.english: “Handle any other introductions among yourselves during your breaks. That is all.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、よろしくお願いします……いえ、こちらこそです……はい、ありがとうございます……」
lines.english: “Oh, nice to meet you... No, the pleasure is mine... Yes, thank you...”

lines.japanese: 同年代の男女たちがよこしてくれた短い挨拶にひとつずつ笑顔を返していると、マスターが俺の体を押してカウンターの外へと追いやろうとします。
lines.english: As I returned each brief greeting from the young men and women with a smile, the boss pushed me bodily out from behind the counter.

lines.japanese: 「鷲介、まだ空いているとはいえ一応お客の目がある。とりあえず仕事着に着替えてこい」
lines.english: “Shusuke, it may still be quiet, but customers are watching. Go and change into your uniform.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、はい。えーと、それは……」
lines.english: “Yes. Um, where would I...?”

lines.japanese: どこでどのように、と途方に暮れている俺を置いて、マスターはたまたま目の前を横切った紀奈子さんに声をかけました。
lines.english: Leaving me at a loss as to where I was supposed to go or what I was supposed to do, the boss called to Kinako as she passed.

lines.japanese: 「望月君。玉泉君はまだ入っていないのかね」
lines.english: “Mochizuki. Has Tamaizumi not arrived yet?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、はい、まだみたいです。もう学校終わってるころだから、そろそろだとは思うんですけど」
lines.english: “No, not yet. School should be out by now, though, so I think she’ll be here soon.”

lines.japanese: 「そうか。ありがとう」
lines.english: “I see. Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 仕事に戻る紀奈子さん。腕を組んで考えこむマスター。
lines.english: Kinako returned to work. The boss folded his arms and considered the matter.

lines.japanese: 「むぅ、どうしたものか。夕方組同士、彼女をトレーナーに付けるつもりだったんだが……」
lines.english: “Hmm. What to do? Since they're both on the evening shift, I had meant to assign her as his trainer...”

lines.japanese: マスターの視線は紀奈子さんの後ろ姿から入り口のドアへ移り、天井を経由して、ふたたび俺に戻ってきました。
lines.english: The boss’s gaze moved from Kinako’s retreating back to the entrance, traveled by way of the ceiling, and returned to me.

lines.japanese: 「ふむ……まあ、鷲介なら案内の必要もないか」
lines.english: “Hmm... Well, Shusuke hardly needs a tour.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ」
lines.english: “Uh-huh.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえ、たしか二階のスタッフルームには入ったことあったよな」
lines.english: “You have been in the second-floor staff room before, haven’t you?”

lines.japanese: そこへ行け、という風に彼は頭上に人差し指を突きたてました。
lines.english: He thrust one index finger toward the ceiling, telling me without words to go upstairs.

lines.japanese: 「当支店には一階と二階、合わせてふたつのスタッフルームがある。鷲介、おまえが使うことになるのは二階の方だ」
lines.english: “This branch has two staff rooms, one on each floor. You will use the room upstairs.”

lines.japanese: 「そこにおまえの名札の付いたロッカーがある。中にウェイター用の制服が入っているから、まずはそれに着替えてきてくれ」
lines.english: “You’ll find a locker there with your name on it. Your waiter’s uniform is inside. Change into it first.”

lines.japanese: 「はい。分かりました」
lines.english: “Yes. Understood.”

lines.japanese: 「言っておくが、くれぐれも初出勤にありがちなアクシデントを装って女子のロッカーを開けたりするなよ」
lines.english: “I should warn you: whatever you do, don't fake one of those classic first-day accidents and open one of the girls' lockers.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ」
lines.english: “Uh-huh.”

lines.japanese: 「ましてや気付かぬ振りを続けて、匂いを嗅いだり袖を通したりなどは言語道断だからな。まあ、そんな非合法の橋を渡らずとも、女子の制服が欲しいと言う希望があるなら実費で譲ってやる。遠慮なく相談しろ」
lines.english: “And needless to say, pretending not to notice your mistake while you sniff the clothes or slip them on would be beyond the pale. If what you want is a women's uniform, however, I'll sell you one at cost. No need to cross the bridge into crime. Come talk to me anytime.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ」
lines.english: “Uh-huh.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふふ、それとも新品では意味がないのかな？」
lines.english: “Heh heh. Or would a brand-new one defeat the purpose?”

lines.japanese: 「……えーと」
「ははは、おい見ろよ。鷲介のやつ、図星を突かれてうろたえていやがるぜ」
lines.english: “Ha! Look at him squirm. Struck a nerve, did I?”

lines.japanese: 「……あのう、すいません、自分もう行っていいすか」
lines.english: “...Um, excuse me. Can I go now?”

lines.japanese: 「ふん……おまえのノリの悪さには幻滅の念を禁じえんな」
lines.english: “Hmph. I cannot help but be dismayed by your refusal to play along.”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、仕事しないでいいんなら、いくらでも乗っかりますけど」
lines.english: “If I don't actually have to work, I'll play along as long as you like.”

lines.japanese: 「ちっ。やむを得ん、行け」
lines.english: “Tch. Very well. Go.”

lines.japanese: 「はい、失礼します！」
lines.english: “Yes, sir. Excuse me!”

lines.japanese: 俺は頭を下げて、愉快な上司のもとを離れました。
lines.english: I bowed and left my delightful superior behind.

lines.japanese: いろいろな意味で、学ぶことの多そうな職場です。
lines.english: This promised to be a workplace with a great deal to teach me, in all sorts of ways.

lines.japanese: ──と金色で書かれたマホガニー調の扉。
lines.english: —written in gold across a mahogany-patterned door.

lines.japanese: 関係者以外の立ち入りを禁じられた区域ですが、そうかぁ今日から俺は関係者なんだよなぁ、なんてちょっとある種の感慨が込みあげてきました。
lines.english: The area beyond was off-limits to unauthorized persons. Realizing that, as of today, I counted as authorized brought on a small but peculiar swell of emotion.

lines.japanese: とりあえずノックしてみます。
lines.english: First, I tried knocking.

lines.japanese: し──ん。
lines.english: Not—a—sound.

lines.japanese: 返事はありません。
lines.english: There was no answer.

lines.japanese: 「失礼しまーす」
lines.english: “Excuse me.”

lines.japanese: それでも一応、礼儀正しげな独り言をつぶやきながらドアを開け、俺は無人の部屋へと──
lines.english: Even so, I opened the door while murmuring that politely phrased soliloquy, and stepped into the empty room—

lines.japanese: ──って、無人じゃねえええー！
lines.english: —WHICH WASN'T EMPTYYYY!

lines.japanese: 「な、ななな……なにごとっ……！？」
lines.english: “Wh-wh-wh... what is going on...?!”

lines.japanese: 合皮のソファーに横たわる、白さもまばゆい女体がひとつ。
lines.english: One dazzlingly white female body lay stretched across the imitation-leather sofa.

lines.japanese: しかも女の子。しかも知ってるひと。しかもパンツ見えてます。
lines.english: A girl, moreover. Somebody I knew, moreover. And her panties were showing, moreover.

lines.japanese: ……ぱんつ？
lines.english: ...Panties?
“Pan—”

lines.japanese: 突然の事態に混乱しつつも、とりあえず俺は自らの口を塞ぎました。
lines.english: Confused by the sudden turn of events, I at least managed to clamp a hand over my own mouth.

lines.japanese: ぱ、ぱぱぱぱんつ、いや、パンツはいい。いいから落ちつけ。落ちつけ俺。ここで騒いだらまた妙な誤解をされかねない。落ちついて対処しよう。
lines.english: P-p-p-panties—no, forget the panties. Calm down. Calm down, me. If I made a scene here, I might invite another bizarre misunderstanding. I had to handle this calmly.

lines.japanese: そう、落ちついて、えーと……えー、どうしたらいいんだ、この状況は。
lines.english: Yes. Calmly. Now, um... what exactly was I supposed to do in this situation?

lines.japanese: ただちにここから立ちさるのがもっとも紳士的でスマートだけれど、あいにくいまの俺には、この部屋でユニフォームに着替えて労働の準備をしなくてはならない義務があります。
lines.english: Leaving at once would be the most gentlemanly and graceful course. Unfortunately, I was presently obliged to change into my uniform in this room and prepare for work.

lines.japanese: だから、まずは安らかに眠る日和子さんを──
lines.english: Therefore, first I would have to deal with the peacefully sleeping Hiyoko—
